To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
amphiphilic OCMC-g-PEG-DDAs self-assembled into micelles in aqueous solution.

the amphiphilic OCMC-g-PEG-DDAs self-assembled into spherical core/shell micelles in aqueous solution, and the size and compactness of the micelles were affected by the ratio of DAA and PEG chains in the graft copolymer.
amphiphilic cellulose graft copolymeres with PEG and DDA as hydrophilic and hydrophobic segments, respectively, were prepared and their self-assembly in aqueoussolution were characterized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a series of amphiphilics with a hydrophobic block and a hydrophilic block.

the preparation of a series of amphiphilics with tunable hydrophilic-hydrophobic balance by grafting a hydrophobic chain on the hydrophilic backbone, which could be used as a novel class of self-assembling materials.
the preparation and characterization of amphiphilie graft copolymeric surfactants from oxidized carboymethyelcellulose and their self-assembly into micelles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the self-assembly behavior of these graft copolymeric amphiphiles in aqueous solution is governed by the balance between hydrophilic and hydrophobic interactions.
the DDA chains are located on the surface of micelles and the PEG chains form a hydrophilic shell.
the amphiphilic OCMC-g-PEG-DDAs self-assemble into micelles in aqueous solution and the core-shell structure of the micelles can be adjusted by the amount of DDA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the self-assembly in aqueoussolution of the amphiphilic copolymers can be controlled by the ratio of DPA and PEG chains and the interfacial compact of the nanoaggregates can be tuned by the content of DDA in the copolymers.
the self-assembly of the amphiphilic grafted copolymers was mainly governed by the ratio of the hydrophobic to hydrophilic moieties, and the hydrophilicity of the copolymers.
the graft copolypeptides with different DDA content could form stable micelles with narrow size distribution and the core/shell interfacial compact was dependent on the DDA content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the self-assembled micelles of the OCMC-g-PEG-DDAs can be used as a template to prepare nanoscale hollow spheres.
the graft copolypeptides from OCMC and PEG-DDA could be self-assembled to form stable and uniform nanomicelles in aqueous solution.
the amphiphilic PEG-OCMC copolymers are capable of self-assembling into stable and well-defined micelles in aqueous solution.
